 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that, on 30.12.2021 at about 9.00 a.m., when the deceased was left his house for painting work from Dasanapura to Makli, he was standing on the footpath near One Body Builder, 2 nd Gate, Makli, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, at that time one Container Tempo goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-A-5777 drove it in a rash &
negligent manner with high speed and dashed to deceased who was standing on footpath.
As a result the deceased fell down and the rear wheel of the Tempo ran over on the head of the deceased, due to impact he died on the spot itself.
It is submitted that postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.

It is submitted that prior to the accident,
the deceased was hale and healthy, and was working as painter and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.

It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of Container Tempo and as such both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
3. In pursuance of duly service of notice, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Court.
Hence he placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Tempo goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-A-5777.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its offending vehicle is denied by this respondent.
Per contra it is alleged that the accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased as he was walking on the road unmindful and without observing the traffic rules.
Hence he is the main architect for the unfortunate accident.
Non -compliance of section's 134(c), 158(6), 147 and 149 of MV Act is pleaded.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.

On account of willful breach of the terms &
conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Rest of the petition averments are contended as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that on 30.12.2021 at about 9.00 a.m. the deceased by name Venkatesh was standing on footpath near A One Body builder, 2nd Gate,
Makali, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru District, at that time,

The parties are also not at variance with regard to the factum of the death of the deceased due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
The conflict is with respect to actionable negligence.
The petitioners plead that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of insured vehicle.
Whereas the Insurance Company contends that the accident in question occurred because of negligence of the deceased.

investigated the matter and laid charge sheet (Ex.P.10) against the driver of insured vehicle for the offences punishable under section's 279, 304(A) of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Further more the careful perusal of Ex.P.3 and 4 being Spot Mahazar and Spot Sketch it reflects that the accident happened when the deceased was walking on the left side of the footpath road,
near one Body Builder, 2 nd Gate, Makali, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru.
It is further shows that the accident occured on the edge of the footpath road.
If the driver of Container Tempo was coming in a normal speed then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Above all even the charge sheet was also filed as against the driver of the offending vehicle.
This Court is aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.3 & 4 which were read in consonance with the Ex.P.10 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is an rash & negligent act of the driver of the Container Tempo.
11. The respondent No.1 who denied negligence on the part of the driver of Container Tempo and contended that the deceased had contributed to the accident, have not led any evidence to this effect.
Further respondent No.1 taken up the contention that the deceased was under intoxication stated and that has contributed for the accident.

He reiterated the contents of written statement filed by respondent No.1.
He has produced Ex.R.1 being the FSL Report the detected level of alcohol in his blood was 56.442mg/100ml of blood.
13. Added more in charge sheet there is absolutely nothing has been whispered by the IO.
The IO has also not invoked sec.185 of MV Act.
Moreover during the course of cross examination RW.1 denied that the accident occurred due to negligence of deceased.
He further admitted that the accident occurred due to the negligence of insured vehicle.

Anyhow the deceased being under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident, by itself would not lead to an automatic inference that he contributed to the cause of accident as a matter of course.
But what cannot be overlooked is that if a person drives a vehicle after taking alcohol and being under its influence, he is likely to expose others to serious risk of accident.
To put it differently, a drunken driver is a potential murderer as he cannot perform his tasks without risks and endangers road safety.

This is so because after drinking,
the judgment power of the driver gets impaired due to which he tends to take more risks, becomes more aggressive and takes a longer reaction time.
In the present case the deceased was not driving the vehicle, but he was pedestrian and walking on the footpath.
Hence the contentions urged by the respondent No.1 does not hold any water in the eye of law.
14. Mere taking up of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the evidence led by the petitioners.

Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the driver of Tempo goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-A-5777.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2 :
The petitioners claim that petitioner No.1 is the mother and petitioner No.2 is the married sister of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit-in-lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards marked at Ex's.P.12 to 13 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
This Court will not loose sight of the fact that the petitioner No.1 is the mother and petitioner No.2 is the married sister of deceased.
The cross examiantoin of PW.1 she admitted that petitioner No.2 is the married but her husband had left her.
Further the petitioner No.2 has not divorced her husband.
When such is the case she is not dependent of the income of the deceased.
Petitoner No.1 being the mother of the deceased was the sole dependent of the deceased earning.
Therefore, from the foregoing reasons it is clearly forthcoming that only petitioner No.1 is the dependent and legal heir of the deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answer to issue No.1 Partly In the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE NO.3:
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
The petitioners contended that, deceased was working as painter and earning of Rs.20,000/-p.m.
However neither the avocation and income of the deceased is substantiated by producing cogent materials nor any witness is examined in this regard.

It is relevant to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 30.12.2021.
Therefore, Rs.15,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

sentences.text: So far as the age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P14 wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 14.07.1985, which indicates that he was aged (36 years 5 months 16 days) 36 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '15'.
18.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 36 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased aged about 36 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.21,000/- p.m. (Rs.15,000 +
6,000/- i.e. 40%).
19.
Further as stated above the deceased was a bachelor, as per the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla verma V/s.
Delhi Transport Corporation

, the 50% of the income of the deceased shall be deducted towards his personal expenses as the deceased unmarried, thereby the 50% income of the deceased has to be deducted for his personal expenditure.

On such deduction,
the income of the deceased comes to Rs.10,500/- p.m. (Rs.21,000 X 50/100).
20. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.10,500/- p.m. and the multiplier '15' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.18,90,000/- (Rs.10,500 X 12 X 15)

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.18,90,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

21. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.

22. In this case, petitioner No.1 is the mother of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner is entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.

24. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
25. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the offending Container Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA-52-A-5777 thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

However the respondent No.1 being a insurer of the offending container tempo is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
26. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
